lesson.title: The Future & the Would-World
lesson.subtitle: gaan + infinitive for plans; zou for the polite conditional

hook.title: Going To and Would
hook.content: Dutch has two futures: gaan + infinitive for plans (ik ga morgen werken) and zullen for promises or predictions (wij zullen komen). The polite conditional is zou, the past of zullen.

pattern.title: Plan with gaan, promise with zullen, soften with zou
pattern.content: Gaan is the everyday 'going to': ik ga werken. Zullen is more formal or predictive: het zal regenen. Zou softens a request: ik zou graag willen.
pattern.linguist_note: Zullen is cognate with English shall; its past zou supplies the polite conditional, much as English would does.
pattern.trap_note: Do not use zou as a past tense of going. Zou is the conditional/polite form; the past of gaan is ging.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (The Future & the Would-World):
exercises.target_answer: gaan, zullen, zou, willen, de morgen, graag
exercises.meaning: to go, will (future), would, to want, tomorrow; morning, gladly; please
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "The Future & the Would-World": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “I am going to work tomorrow.”?
exercises.meaning: I am going to work tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: “Ik ga morgen werken.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “The Future & the Would-World”.

cues: The pattern: Plan with gaan, promise with zullen, soften with zou
exercises.explanation: “Wij zullen komen.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Plan with gaan, promise with zullen, soften with zou.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not use zou as a past tense of going. Zou is the conditional/polite form; the past of gaan is ging.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Ik zou graag willen.” is word-for-word “I would gladly want.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Plan with gaan, promise with zullen, soften with zou.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.meaning: He is going to make it.
cues: It means: He is going to make it.
exercises.explanation: “Hij gaat het maken.” reuses only material taught in “The Future & the Would-World” — Plan with gaan, promise with zullen, soften with zou.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Hij gaat het maken.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Plan with gaan, promise with zullen, soften with zou.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I would like to go.”
twist.explanation: Zou + graag softens the wish; the infinitive gaan stays at the end.

summary.outcome: Talk about plans with gaan, predictions with zullen, and polite wishes with zou.

use_example.english: He is going to make it.

summary.takeaway: Dutch future is a choice of stance: going to, will, or would.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Future & Would Gym.

gaan.etymology_derivation: The same verb as English go, with the old g still pronounced.

zullen.etymology_derivation: English shall and Dutch zullen are the same modal root.

zou.etymology_derivation: The past form of zullen, used for polite conditionals.

willen.etymology_derivation: English will (as desire) and Dutch willen are the same verb.

morgen.etymology_derivation: English morrow and Dutch morgen are the same word.

graag.etymology_derivation: The adverb of willingness; Dutch uses it where English says 'like to'.
